records.title: Mesopotamia: Sumer, Akkad, Babylon and Assyria
records.summary: Several societies flourished around the Tigris and Euphrates; Mesopotamia is a historical region, not a present-day country.
facts: Sumerian cities developed early cuneiform writing.
Babylon and Nineveh were distinct centres.
Modern-country tags indicate regional overlap, not exclusive ownership.

records.title: Ancient Egypt
records.summary: A long-lived Nile-centred civilisation with changing kingdoms and dynasties.
facts: Hieroglyphs are an Egyptian writing system.
Upper Egypt lies south of Lower Egypt.
Pyramids and the Rosetta Stone are useful location and history connections.

records.title: Indus / Harappan civilisation
records.summary: Urban Bronze Age societies across parts of present-day Pakistan and northwestern India.
facts: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are key sites.
Its script remains undeciphered.
The mature urban phase is narrower than the entire settlement history.

records.title: Minoan civilisation
records.summary: Bronze Age civilisation associated especially with Crete.
facts: Knossos is a major palace site.
Do not confuse Minoan Crete with mainland Mycenaean centres.
Dates vary by archaeological phase.

records.title: Ancient Greece
records.period: Archaic and Classical periods c. 800–323 BCE
records.summary: Greek-speaking communities and city-states extended beyond the borders of present-day Greece.
facts: Athens and Sparta were separate city-states.
Socrates, Plato and Aristotle are distinct philosophers.
Greek settlements also existed in Anatolia and around the Mediterranean.

records.title: Ancient Rome
records.summary: Roman political institutions changed from republic to empire and ruled a much wider region than modern Italy.
facts: Rome is the founding urban centre.
The western imperial government conventionally ends in 476 CE.
The eastern Roman / Byzantine state continued until 1453.

records.title: Maya civilisation
records.summary: Maya societies developed in Mesoamerica; Maya peoples and languages continue today.
facts: Tikal is in Guatemala; Chichen Itza is in Mexico.
The end of the Classic period did not mean the disappearance of Maya peoples.
Maya writing and calendar systems are study themes.

records.title: Inca civilisation
records.summary: The Inca state expanded across much of the Andes, with Cusco as a major centre.
facts: Machu Picchu is in present-day Peru.
Andean road networks connected different ecological zones.
Inca is not a synonym for all Indigenous peoples of South America.

records.title: Khmer / Angkor civilisation
records.summary: A major mainland Southeast Asian civilisation centred on the Angkor region.
facts: Angkor is in modern Cambodia.
Angkor Wat and Angkor Thom are different complexes.
Historic regional influence does not define current national borders.

records.title: Ancient Bengal: Pundra and Varendra
records.summary: Ancient Bengal contained multiple regional identities and political centres.
facts: Mahasthangarh is associated with ancient Pundranagara.
Paharpur is a major Buddhist monastic site.
Historical Bengal is broader than modern Bangladesh.

records.title: Aksum civilisation
records.summary: A Red Sea-connected civilisation in the northern Horn of Africa.
facts: Aksum is in modern Ethiopia.
Trade linked the Horn of Africa with the Red Sea world.
The civilisation’s region also relates to present-day Eritrea.

records.title: Great Zimbabwe
records.summary: A major southern African stone-built urban and trading centre.
facts: The site lies in modern Zimbabwe.
Dry-stone architecture is a distinctive feature.
The archaeological site should be distinguished from the modern state.

records.title: Mukti Bahini
records.summary: Bangladesh liberation forces during the 1971 Liberation War, including regular and irregular formations.
facts: Study the Bangladesh Liberation War context.
This is a historical umbrella term, not a current organisation.
Avoid treating every liberation formation as the same organisation.

records.title: Viet Minh
records.summary: Vietnamese independence movement associated with Ho Chi Minh and the struggle against colonial rule.
facts: Viet Minh and Viet Cong are different labels.
Dien Bien Phu is associated with 1954.
Its historical setting includes Japanese occupation and French colonial rule.

records.title: Viet Cong / National Liberation Front
records.summary: The National Liberation Front was a political and armed movement in South Vietnam.
facts: Do not equate the Viet Cong with the earlier Viet Minh.
Study it within the Vietnam War.
The entry describes the historical organisation, not contemporary Vietnam.

records.title: FLN: Algerian National Liberation Front
records.summary: A central organisation in Algeria’s independence struggle against French colonial rule.
facts: FLN is the French acronym of Front de liberation nationale.
Armed-struggle history and later party politics are separate phases.
Algerian independence is associated with 1962.

records.title: Mau Mau / Kenya Land and Freedom Army
records.summary: An anti-colonial armed movement in Kenya; the name encompasses a complicated historical movement.
facts: Dedan Kimathi is an associated historical figure.
The emergency is associated with British colonial Kenya.
Current Kenyan state institutions are separate from this movement.

records.title: Umkhonto we Sizwe (MK)
records.summary: The historical armed wing associated with the African National Congress during the anti-apartheid struggle.
facts: Nelson Mandela was among its founders.
Historical MK and later political parties using similar names must be distinguished.
Read it in the apartheid and transition-to-democracy context.

records.title: FARC: historical armed organisation
records.summary: A Colombian insurgent organisation whose principal demobilisation was associated with the 2016 peace agreement.
facts: The main peace agreement and subsequent dissident groups are separate subjects.
Do not infer today’s legal status from this historical entry.
Colombia is the country association.

records.title: LTTE: Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam
records.summary: A separatist armed organisation associated with Sri Lanka’s civil war.
facts: Velupillai Prabhakaran was its founder.
The conventional military defeat occurred in 2009.
This historical record does not describe the views of all Sri Lankan Tamil people.

records.title: Provisional IRA
records.summary: An Irish republican paramilitary organisation associated with the Northern Ireland conflict.
facts: Different organisations have used the IRA name.
The 1998 Belfast / Good Friday Agreement is a separate peace-settlement topic.
Republican political parties and armed organisations should not be conflated.

records.title: Sandinista National Liberation Front
records.summary: A Nicaraguan movement that later became a governing political party.
facts: FSLN is its Spanish acronym.
Its historical movement phase and current party politics are different.
The Contras were opposing armed groups, not another name for the Sandinistas.

records.title: Bangladesh: constitutional foreign-relations principles
records.summary: Article 25 provides the constitutional principles underlying Bangladesh’s international relations.
facts: Respect for sovereignty and equality.
Non-interference and peaceful dispute settlement.
Respect for international law and UN Charter principles.
Distinguish the constitutional framework from a government’s changing diplomatic choices.

records.title: Monroe Doctrine
records.summary: A US policy statement opposing new European colonisation and intervention in the Western Hemisphere.
facts: Associated with President James Monroe.
Later interpretations and interventions changed its practical meaning.
It is a historical doctrine, not a treaty.

records.title: Truman Doctrine
records.summary: A US commitment to support Greece and Türkiye that became a major early Cold War policy statement.
facts: Associated with Harry S. Truman.
Study containment as its Cold War context.
Do not confuse it with the Marshall Plan.

records.title: Marshall Plan
records.summary: A US-backed European recovery programme after the Second World War.
facts: Associated with George C. Marshall.
Economic recovery differs from NATO’s collective-defence purpose.
Recipient-country lists and wartime alliances are different datasets.

records.title: Panchsheel / Five Principles
records.summary: Five principles associated with India–China relations and broader peaceful-coexistence diplomacy.
facts: Mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit.
Peaceful coexistence.
A doctrine does not prove that actual relations always follow it.

records.title: Non-Aligned Movement
records.summary: A movement associated with avoiding alignment with the principal Cold War power blocs.
facts: Belgrade hosted the first summit.
Non-alignment is not identical to legal neutrality.
This entry tags key founding contexts, not the entire present membership.

records.title: Bandung Conference
records.summary: An Asian–African conference important to decolonisation and later non-aligned cooperation.
facts: Held in Bandung, Indonesia.
Bandung 1955 and Belgrade 1961 are distinct events.
It involved Asian and African states, not a worldwide military alliance.

records.title: Ostpolitik
records.summary: West German policy associated with improving relations with Eastern Europe during the Cold War.
facts: Closely associated with Willy Brandt.
Study it as a West German historical policy.
It is not a present-day universal German foreign-policy label.

records.title: Neutrality and non-alignment: distinction
records.summary: Neutrality, non-alignment and membership in a military alliance are different concepts.
facts: Switzerland’s neutrality has a specific legal and historical context.
Austria’s neutrality framework differs from Switzerland’s.
NATO membership is shown separately in the organisation filter.

records.title: Montreal Protocol
records.summary: Protects the ozone layer through control of ozone-depleting substances.
facts: Montreal is in Canada.
Do not confuse ozone depletion with climate change.
A global agreement: the Canada tag marks the adoption venue, not the only participant.

records.title: Kyoto Protocol
records.summary: A climate agreement under the UNFCCC with quantified commitments for specified developed-country parties.
facts: Kyoto is in Japan.
The 1997 adoption and 2005 entry into force are different.
Compare its framework with the Paris Agreement.

records.title: Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety
records.summary: Addresses the safe transfer, handling and use of living modified organisms under the CBD.
facts: Adopted in Montreal despite its Cartagena name.
Cartagena is in Colombia.
Country tags mark name / venue context, not all parties.

records.title: Nagoya Protocol
records.summary: Addresses access to genetic resources and the sharing of benefits from their use.
facts: Nagoya is in Japan.
Associated with the Convention on Biological Diversity.
Do not confuse it with Cartagena’s biosafety subject.

records.title: Geneva Protocol
records.summary: Prohibits the use in war of asphyxiating, poisonous or other gases and bacteriological methods of warfare.
facts: The 1925 protocol is distinct from the four 1949 Geneva Conventions.
Production and stockpile prohibitions are addressed in later weapons conventions.

records.title: Additional Protocols I and II
records.summary: Supplement the 1949 Geneva Conventions for international and non-international armed conflicts.
facts: Protocol I concerns international armed conflict.
Protocol II concerns specified non-international armed conflicts.
Do not merge them with the 1925 Geneva Protocol.

records.title: Kigali Amendment
records.summary: An amendment to the Montreal Protocol concerning the phasedown of HFCs.
facts: Kigali is in Rwanda.
HFCs are powerful greenhouse gases.
It is an amendment, not a separate protocol.

records.title: UN Charter
records.summary: The foundational treaty of the United Nations.
facts: Signed in San Francisco.
UN Day is 24 October.
The Charter includes the framework for the Security Council and peaceful settlement.

records.title: Paris Agreement
records.summary: Global climate framework under the UNFCCC.
facts: Adopted at COP21 in Paris.
Nationally determined contributions are central to its framework.
Venue tagging does not assert a complete parties list.

records.title: UNFCCC
records.summary: Framework convention for international cooperation on climate change.
facts: Opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit.
Kyoto and Paris are instruments within its broader regime.

records.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
records.summary: Addresses biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, and benefit sharing.
facts: Rio Earth Summit connection.
Cartagena and Nagoya are protocols to the CBD.

records.title: Ramsar Convention
facts: Ramsar is a city in Iran.
World Wetlands Day is 2 February.
Wetland listing and national sovereignty are separate matters.

records.title: CITES
records.summary: Regulates international trade in specimens of listed wild fauna and flora.
facts: Signed in Washington, DC.
Different appendices have different controls.
CITES is not a general ban on all wildlife trade.

records.title: UNCLOS
records.period: Opened for signature 10 December 1982; in force 16 November 1994
records.summary: A broad framework for the law of the sea.
facts: Montego Bay signing context.
Territorial sea up to 12 nautical miles; EEZ up to 200 nautical miles from baselines.
Overlapping entitlements may require delimitation.

records.title: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations
records.summary: Framework for diplomatic relations, privileges and immunities.
facts: Diplomatic relations differ from consular relations.
Diplomatic immunity is not a statement that conduct is lawful.

records.title: Vienna Convention on Consular Relations
records.summary: Framework for consular relations and functions.
facts: 1963 consular convention differs from the 1961 diplomatic convention.
Consular protection and diplomatic representation are distinct.

records.title: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties
facts: Pacta sunt servanda concerns performance in good faith.
Do not confuse this convention with the two Vienna diplomatic / consular conventions.

records.title: Four Geneva Conventions
records.summary: Core humanitarian treaties protecting specified victims of armed conflict.
facts: Convention III addresses prisoners of war.
Convention IV addresses civilians.
Additional Protocols are separate instruments.

records.title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)
records.period: Opened for signature 1968; in force 5 March 1970
records.summary: Nuclear non-proliferation, disarmament and peaceful-use framework.
facts: Three depositary governments: US, UK and the Soviet Union / Russia.
NPT, CTBT and TPNW are different treaties.

records.title: Chemical Weapons Convention
records.period: Opened for signature 1993; in force 29 April 1997
records.summary: Prohibits chemical weapons and provides a verification regime.
facts: OPCW is based in The Hague.
Paris is the signature-venue context.
Distinguish OPCW from the IAEA.

records.title: Biological Weapons Convention
records.period: Opened for signature 1972; in force 26 March 1975
records.summary: Prohibits specified biological and toxin weapons activities.
facts: Distinct from the Chemical Weapons Convention.
The 1925 Geneva Protocol addresses use in war.

records.title: Rome Statute of the ICC
records.summary: Founding treaty of the International Criminal Court.
facts: Adopted in Rome; the Court is in The Hague.
ICC prosecutes individuals; ICJ principally addresses interstate disputes.

records.title: Treaty of Versailles
records.summary: One of the post-First World War peace treaties, addressing Germany.
facts: The 1918 armistice and 1919 peace treaty are different.
Other defeated powers had different peace treaties.

records.title: Treaty of Westphalia: peace settlements
records.summary: Peace settlements associated with ending the Thirty Years War and wider European conflicts.
facts: Munster and Osnabruck are key negotiating locations.
The modern sovereign-state narrative is an interpretation, not a single clause creating all states.

records.title: Indus Waters Treaty
records.summary: An India–Pakistan river-water arrangement with the World Bank’s specified role.
facts: Historical allocation distinguishes eastern and western river groups.
Recent implementation disputes require current sources.
This record is not a claim that diplomatic conditions are unchanged.

records.title: India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement
records.summary: Land-boundary arrangements including the exchange of enclaves.
facts: 111 Indian and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves were exchanged.
The 1974 agreement date is different from 2015 implementation.

records.title: Belfast / Good Friday Agreement
records.summary: A peace-settlement framework for Northern Ireland.
facts: Includes political institutions and British–Irish relationships.
It is distinct from earlier ceasefires.

facts: Author: Plato
Political philosophy and justice; not a modern constitution.
records.author: Plato

records.title: Politics
facts: Author: Aristotle
Political communities and constitutions; distinguish it from Plato’s Republic.
records.author: Aristotle

records.title: The Prince
facts: Author: Niccolo Machiavelli
Political power and statecraft; writing and publication dates differ.
records.author: Niccolo Machiavelli

records.title: Utopia
facts: Author: Thomas More
Political and social thought; the title also became a general term.
records.author: Thomas More

records.title: Leviathan
facts: Author: Thomas Hobbes
Sovereignty and the social contract.
records.author: Thomas Hobbes

records.title: Two Treatises of Government
facts: Author: John Locke
Government, rights and consent.
records.author: John Locke

records.title: The Spirit of the Laws
facts: Author: Montesquieu
Political institutions and the separation of powers.
records.author: Montesquieu

records.title: The Social Contract
facts: Author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
Popular sovereignty and political legitimacy.
records.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau

records.title: The Wealth of Nations
facts: Author: Adam Smith
Political economy; the complete title is An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations.
records.author: Adam Smith

records.title: The Communist Manifesto
facts: Author: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels
A jointly authored political text; both authors matter in matching questions.
records.author: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels

records.title: Das Kapital, Volume I
facts: Author: Karl Marx
Political economy; later volumes were edited and published by Friedrich Engels.
records.author: Karl Marx

records.title: On the Origin of Species
facts: Author: Charles Darwin
Evolution by natural selection; a science-history connection.
records.author: Charles Darwin

records.title: The Art of War
facts: Author: Traditionally attributed to Sun Tzu
Attribution and dating are traditional; it is not a modern national defence policy.
records.author: Traditionally attributed to Sun Tzu

records.title: Gitanjali
facts: Author: Rabindranath Tagore
Different language editions have different dates; Tagore won Literature in 1913.
records.author: Rabindranath Tagore

records.title: The Discovery of India
facts: Author: Jawaharlal Nehru
History and reflections written during imprisonment.
records.author: Jawaharlal Nehru

records.title: An Autobiography: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
facts: Author: M. K. Gandhi
Autobiography; translation and book editions vary.
records.author: M. K. Gandhi

records.title: Long Walk to Freedom
facts: Author: Nelson Mandela
Autobiography associated with the anti-apartheid struggle.
records.author: Nelson Mandela

records.title: The Second World War
facts: Author: Winston Churchill
A multi-volume historical work; not a single-volume publication in one year.
records.author: Winston Churchill

records.title: The Diary of a Young Girl
facts: Author: Anne Frank
A diary from the Holocaust era, published posthumously; editions vary.
records.author: Anne Frank

facts: Author: George Orwell
Dystopian novel; publication year is different from the title’s year.
records.author: George Orwell

records.title: Animal Farm
facts: Author: George Orwell
Political allegory; distinguish the book from 1984.
records.author: George Orwell

records.title: Things Fall Apart
facts: Author: Chinua Achebe
Novel associated with Igbo society and colonial change.
records.author: Chinua Achebe

records.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
facts: Author: Gabriel Garcia Marquez
Latin American novel; Spanish publication date.
records.author: Gabriel Garcia Marquez

records.title: The Old Man and the Sea
facts: Author: Ernest Hemingway
Novel set around Cuba; setting does not make the author Cuban.
records.author: Ernest Hemingway

records.title: Banker to the Poor
facts: Author: Muhammad Yunus with Alan Jolis
Microfinance memoir; editions and translations vary.
records.author: Muhammad Yunus with Alan Jolis

records.title: The Unfinished Memoirs
facts: Author: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
Posthumously published autobiographical writings.
records.author: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman

records.title: Alfred Nobel
records.summary: Inventor and founder whose will established the Nobel Prizes.
facts: Economics is a later memorial prize, first awarded in 1969.

records.title: Rabindranath Tagore
records.summary: Bengali writer; Nobel Prize in Literature 1913.
facts: Author of the lyrics of India’s and Bangladesh’s national anthems; historical Bengal spans current borders.

records.title: Muhammad Yunus
records.summary: Microfinance economist; shared the 2006 Peace Prize with Grameen Bank.
facts: The Peace Prize is not an Economics award; current government office is intentionally not inferred.

records.title: Nelson Mandela
records.summary: Anti-apartheid leader; shared the 1993 Peace Prize.
facts: His historical role, Nobel award and presidency are separate study facts.

records.title: Mahatma Gandhi
records.summary: Leader associated with nonviolent resistance in India’s independence movement.
facts: He never received a Nobel Prize.

records.title: Marie Curie
records.summary: Physicist and chemist; Nobel awards in Physics 1903 and Chemistry 1911.
facts: Born in Warsaw; worked in France. Birthplace and award affiliation are distinct.

records.title: Albert Einstein
facts: The award citation emphasised the photoelectric effect, not simply relativity.

records.title: Henry Dunant
records.summary: Humanitarian associated with the Red Cross; shared the first Peace Prize in 1901.
facts: ICRC is an organisation; Henry Dunant is a person.

records.title: Woodrow Wilson
records.summary: US president associated with the Fourteen Points and League of Nations.
facts: Awarded the 1919 Peace Prize.

records.title: Winston Churchill
facts: Received the 1953 Literature Prize, not the Peace Prize.

records.title: Ho Chi Minh
facts: Distinguish the Viet Minh independence movement from the Viet Cong.

records.title: Sun Yat-sen
records.summary: Political leader associated with the 1911 Chinese revolution and republican thought.
facts: Historical roles and modern national claims require separate treatment.

records.title: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk
records.summary: Founding president of the Republic of Türkiye.
facts: The Republic was proclaimed in 1923.

records.title: Jawaharlal Nehru
records.summary: India’s first prime minister and an important figure in non-alignment.
facts: Author of The Discovery of India.

records.title: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
records.summary: Central leader of Bangladesh’s independence movement.
facts: The Unfinished Memoirs was published posthumously in 2012.

records.title: Kazi Nazrul Islam
records.summary: Bengali poet and musician, recognised as Bangladesh’s national poet.
facts: Historic Bengal and present-day country labels should not be collapsed.

records.title: Plato
records.summary: Ancient Greek philosopher; author of the Republic.
facts: Socrates was his teacher; Aristotle studied at his Academy.

records.title: Aristotle
records.summary: Ancient Greek philosopher; author of Politics.
facts: Do not attribute the Republic to Aristotle.

records.title: Ibn Khaldun
records.summary: Historian and social thinker associated with the Muqaddimah.
facts: Born in Tunis; his work belongs to a wider North African and Islamic intellectual context.

records.title: Chinua Achebe
records.summary: Nigerian novelist; author of Things Fall Apart.
facts: Achebe did not win the Nobel Prize; Wole Soyinka did.

records.title: First World War: overview
records.summary: A global conflict involving the Central Powers and the Allied / Entente powers.
facts: Austria-Hungary’s declaration of war on Serbia is a conventional opening date.
The 11 November armistice ended fighting on the Western Front; peace treaties followed.
Modern country tags are study links, not complete historical belligerent lists.

records.title: Sarajevo assassination
records.summary: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and Sophie in Sarajevo.
facts: A trigger of the July Crisis; not the sole cause of the war.
Sarajevo is in present-day Bosnia and Herzegovina.

records.title: First World War: alliance distinctions
records.summary: The Central Powers and Entente / Allies were changing wartime coalitions.
facts: Central Powers included Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria.
Italy’s prewar Triple Alliance membership differs from its wartime Allied alignment from 1915.
Russia and the US entered / exited different phases of the conflict.

records.title: Versailles and the League of Nations
records.summary: Postwar peace arrangements and the development of the League of Nations.
facts: The Versailles treaty was signed in 1919, after the 1918 armistice.
The League is distinct from the UN established in 1945.

records.title: Second World War: overview
records.summary: The European war conventionally begins with Germany’s invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939.
facts: Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September.
War in Asia had earlier starting points, including 1937 in China.
Germany’s defeat in May and Japan’s formal surrender in September 1945 are separate endpoints.

records.title: Second World War: Axis and Allies
records.summary: Germany, Italy and Japan were the principal Axis powers; the Allied coalition evolved.
facts: The Soviet Union entered the war against Germany in June 1941.
The US entered after Pearl Harbor in December 1941.
Modern Russia does not stand for every territory or people of the historical USSR.

records.title: Pearl Harbor
records.summary: Japanese attack on the US Pacific Fleet base in Hawaii.
facts: Hawaii is part of the United States.
The attack preceded the US declaration of war on Japan.

records.title: D-Day / Normandy landings
facts: D-Day is not the date the Second World War ended.
Normandy lies in northern France.

records.title: Holocaust
records.summary: Nazi Germany and its collaborators murdered six million European Jews and persecuted other groups.
facts: A central part of Second World War history.
Country tags indicate selected perpetrator / site geography, not collective guilt.

records.title: VE Day and VJ Day
records.summary: Victory-in-Europe commemorations and the end of the war against Japan use different dates.
facts: VE Day is commonly marked on 8 May; some countries commemorate 9 May.
Japan announced acceptance in August; formal surrender was signed on 2 September.
The calendar / time-zone context matters.

records.title: Yalta and Potsdam conferences
records.summary: Major Allied conferences addressing the closing war and postwar arrangements.
facts: Yalta is in Crimea; the country tag is a present-day geographic context with disputed control.
Potsdam is in Germany.
The conferences are not the same event.

records.title: United Nations after the Second World War
records.summary: The UN was created in the aftermath of the war.
facts: Charter signed 26 June 1945 in San Francisco.
Charter entered into force 24 October 1945.
The League of Nations and UN are different organisations.

records.title: Line of Control
records.summary: Military control line in Jammu and Kashmir; not a final international border. Marker is approximate; consult the UN map for the route.
facts: Classification: Military control / position line
LoC and LAC concern different country pairs. Consult UN / agreement maps for the exact Kashmir reference.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

The source uses the generic name “Line of control” for several India–Pakistan segments, including southern Working Boundary context. The overlay must not be read as one exact, agreed LoC route or an agreed extension beyond NJ9842.

records.title: Line of Actual Control
records.summary: India–China control-line concept; alignment is disputed and not mutually agreed in all sectors. Marker gives regional location only.
facts: Classification: Military control / position line
Perceptions of alignment differ in places. No mutually agreed, surveyed LAC route is asserted here.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: McMahon Line
records.summary: Boundary proposed in 1914 in the eastern Himalayas; disputed between India and China. Location marker only.
facts: Classification: Disputed boundary reference
Boundary proposal and actual military control are different concepts.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: Radcliffe Line — west
records.summary: 1947 partition boundary in Punjab; distinguish it from the Line of Control in Kashmir.
facts: Classification: Historical boundary reference
Distinguish the Punjab partition boundary from the Line of Control in Kashmir.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: Radcliffe Line — east
records.summary: 1947 partition boundary in Bengal; later agreements adjusted parts of the India–Bangladesh boundary.
facts: Classification: Historical boundary reference
Subsequent India–Bangladesh land agreements adjusted the modern boundary.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: Durand Line
records.summary: 1893 Afghanistan–British India boundary agreement; associated with the Afghanistan–Pakistan border and contested historically.
facts: Classification: Named boundary / agreement
Historical boundary agreement; not synonymous with a generic Line of Control.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: Korean Demilitarized Zone
records.summary: 1953 armistice zone around the Military Demarcation Line. It does not simply follow the 38th parallel.
facts: Classification: Ceasefire / buffer-zone reference
The DMZ surrounds the MDL; the 38th parallel is a separate historical latitude reference.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: 38th parallel north
records.summary: Historical 1945 division reference for Korea. The present demarcation line differs from this latitude.
facts: Classification: Latitude reference
A parallel is a circle of latitude, not automatically a political or military boundary.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: 49th parallel north
records.summary: Forms much of the western Canada–US boundary, not the entire border.
facts: Classification: Latitude reference
A parallel is a circle of latitude, not automatically a political or military boundary.
Map locators are approximate. Dashed route overlays, where available, are generalised Natural Earth source snapshots; they are not live military positions or surveyed legal limits.

records.title: 17th parallel north
records.summary: Historical reference for the provisional Vietnam division under the 1954 Geneva arrangements; not a current national boundary.
facts: Classification: Latitude reference
A parallel is a circle of latitude, not automatically a political or military boundary.
